slides.headline: Born on September 10th, the man who redrew India's map along language lines.
Govind Ballabh Pant
slides.body: Born in a small village near Almora in the United Provinces, Pant trained as a lawyer before joining India's independence movement alongside Gandhi, Nehru and Patel. He was jailed twice by the British - once for organizing the Satyagraha movement, once for signing the Quit India resolution.

slides.headline: First CM of UP, then the states-reorganization architect.
slides.body: After independence, Pant became Uttar Pradesh's first Chief Minister, abolishing the zamindari land system. As Union Home Minister from 1955, his defining achievement was reorganizing India's states along linguistic lines - the map India still largely uses today.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: Structural decisions outlast the people who make them.
slides.body: Pant received the Bharat Ratna in 1957 and died in office in 1961. Nearly seven decades later, the state boundaries he helped draw still shape how India governs itself - proof that the unglamorous work of institution-building compounds longer than almost anything else.
